ops.title: Formula post_install cannot deliver LaunchAgents: Homebrew sandbox denies ~/Library/LaunchAgents writes — every brew-driven converge fails by design
ops.description:
Field-proven on the local machine 2026-07-26, on captain-hook 12.20.12 + daemonkit v0.20.9: with path resolution fully fixed (the diagnostic names the REAL /Users/yasyf/Library/LaunchAgents path), formula post_install still fails one step earlier — 'service: write agent plist: create temp /Users/yasyf/Library/LaunchAgents/.durable-407643303: operation not permitted'. Homebrew runs formula post_install under a sandbox that denies file-write-create in ~/Library/LaunchAgents at ANY path, so no daemonkit-side fix can make formula postinstall deliver a LaunchAgent. (History: the sandbox's temp-HOME half was the EIO root cause, fixed in daemonkit v0.20.9 — investigation 8841b9c0; the write-denial half is unfixable below the packaging layer.)

WORKING PATH (proven): run the delivered Cellar's 'capt-hookd package-install' from a normal user shell — unsandboxed + real HOME converges cleanly end-to-end (bundle 12.20.12 delivered, sealed receipts, keyless agents bootstrapped, helper status ok=True). ALSO: the 'capt-hook helper install' CLI verb the caveat advertises does NOT converge anything — it checks brew state and prints the caveat.

Fix directions: (a) caveat-only post_install + first-run/host-daemon self-heal owns delivery; (b) ship as a cask (cask postflight runs unsandboxed); (c) wire 'capt-hook helper install' to capt-hookd package-install so the caveat is true. Fleet impact: every machine converging captain-hook via brew hits this — the yasyf-box repair recipe is already amended (fc39f885).

ops.text: brew upgrade/install converges the deployment on a clean machine without manual capt-hookd invocation (delivery moved out of formula postinstall, or packaging switched to a cask whose artifacts run unsandboxed)
capt-hook helper install performs a real converge (currently a no-op wrapper: brew-state check + caveat print) or the caveat names the working command
